title: Long AAPL — WWDC AI + PCC Deal; Post-FOMC Dip Entry at $285-295
entry: CONDITIONAL — Do NOT buy at today's open (~$300). Entry fires only in the $285-295 window on a post-FOMC dip (June 17-19). Specifically: (1) Warsh FOMC press conference June 17 at 2:00 PM ET is neutral or mildly dovish AND (2) AAPL pulls back 1.5-3% from today's session close into $285-295 in the June 17-19 window. Scale: 60% at $292-295 on the first dip; 40% add if AAPL extends to $285-290 intraday with a recovery close above $287. If FOMC is hawkish (30Y rises above 5.05%), the entry is paused — wait for $275-280 re-entry zone instead.
stop_loss: $278 daily close (~4.1% below entry midpoint $290) — implies Warsh FOMC hawkish surprise sends 30Y back above 5.10%, compressing AAPL's multiple; or Apple's Private Cloud Compute (PCC) partnership with Google/NVIDIA faces a regulatory or competitive challenge that removes the Siri AI monetization thesis
targets: $308 — AAPL recovers the pre-FOMC level; Private Cloud Compute Siri integration confirmed in a developer beta showing measurable quality improvement; VIX closes below 15; +6.2% from entry midpoint $290

$320 — AAPL June quarter revenue beat (late July): iPhone cycle driven by AI Siri upgrade demand; Services revenue re-accelerates as Apple Intelligence subscription revenue begins; institutional AI exposure rotation into AAPL as the consumer AI play; +10.3%

$340 — Full AI monetization re-rating: Apple Intelligence + PCC + NVDA Blackwell integration in Apple Silicon confirms AAPL as the 'AI edge computing' platform company, not just a hardware cycle; P/E re-rates from current 29x to 33-35x on durable AI revenue; +17.2%
catalyst: Apple WWDC (June 8) delivered the Apple Intelligence 2.0 update anchored by the Private Cloud Compute (PCC) expansion through Google Cloud + NVIDIA collaboration. The deal — confirmed by Seeking Alpha as AAPL extending PCC via Google's TPU infrastructure with NVDA B200 Blackwell chips — positions Apple as the first consumer hardware company with a hybrid on-device/cloud AI platform at scale. Siri's PCC upgrade enables Apple Intelligence features that were previously hardware-constrained to process on-device, expanding the addressable compute for AI applications by approximately 100-200x per request. AAPL at $300 today is approaching the WWDC-derived level; the regime clearance (Iran deal, VIX below 18, 30Y below 5.00%) removes the macro headwind that compressed AAPL's multiple since April 2026. FOMC June 17 is the final gate before conviction can be raised.
thesis:
AAPL's WWDC AI setup is the most under-appreciated catalyst in the active book. While the market has been focused on NVDA, GOOGL, and MRVL as AI infrastructure plays, AAPL is the AI deployment platform: the company that will monetize AI at the consumer scale no other technology company can access. Apple's installed base of 2.3B active devices — 1.4B iPhones — is the largest distribution network in technology. Every iPhone 15+ and Mac M1+ that receives the iOS 20/macOS 27 update with Apple Intelligence 2.0 becomes an AI-capable endpoint connected to Apple's PCC infrastructure. The PCC extension via Google Cloud + NVDA Blackwell chips (confirmed June 10) means Apple Intelligence can now run models 10-100x larger than on-device silicon allows, without the privacy trade-off of traditional cloud AI (PCC is privacy-preserving by design).

The timing for the FOMC-dip entry is deliberate and important. AAPL at $300 on June 15 is pricing: (1) Iran deal macro relief, (2) WWDC AI catalyst, and (3) regime clearance — but NOT a confirmed neutral Warsh FOMC. If Warsh's June 17 press conference (his first as Fed Chair, without the dot plot as a scaffolding tool) is read as hawkish or ambiguous, tech multiples compress intraday and AAPL falls to $285-295. That pullback is the entry — buying the FOMC risk event when it resolves rather than before. The $278 stop ensures that a genuinely hawkish Warsh outcome (30Y back above 5.10%, VIX re-breaching 18) doesn't create an outsized loss.

The fundamental setup for AAPL's June quarter (reported late July) is the medium-term catalyst. Apple Intelligence 2.0's Siri upgrade is expected to be the primary iPhone 16 upgrade driver heading into the iPhone 17 cycle. Channel checks (Best Buy, Walmart, Target) have been indicating pre-announcement interest in iPhone 16 upgrades from iPhone 13-14 users — the AI feature gap between these devices and the current generation is the largest in iPhone's history. The June quarter Apple Intelligence install base is estimated at 500M+ devices globally. The monetization lever — an Apple Intelligence subscription tier ($4.99-$9.99/month) confirmed in developer documentation — has not yet been reflected in consensus revenue estimates for FY2027.

The counter-party is the AAPL bear who argues: (1) $300 AAPL already trades at 29x forward earnings — the AI monetization is priced in before a single Apple Intelligence subscription has been sold; (2) the PCC Google/NVDA deal is operationally complex and may underdeliver on Siri quality in the first 6-12 months; (3) FOMC June 17 risk is acute for a stock at 29x that has priced both the Iran relief AND the AI catalyst. The conditional entry ($285-295) addresses argument (3) directly — we are specifically buying the post-FOMC dip, not the pre-FOMC level.
bull_case: Warsh FOMC June 17 is neutral or dovish: no explicit hike signal, 30Y falls to 4.80-4.85%. AAPL pulls back 2-2.5% to $293-295 on June 17-18 as FOMC uncertainty resolves. Entry triggered at $293-295. Apple Intelligence Siri PCC quality improvements confirmed in developer beta 2 (late June). June quarter iPhone channel data (IDC/Canalys) shows 12%+ upgrade cycle acceleration. AAPL to $308-320 by mid-July before Q3 earnings.
bear_case: Warsh FOMC hawkish: 'actively monitoring for another hike' language drives 30Y above 5.05%; AAPL falls from $300 to $280-285 without triggering the conditional entry at $285-295 (too fast to scale in cleanly). Entry deferred. If FOMC is neutral but AAPL doesn't pull back (holds $298-302 through June 17-19), the setup expires without triggering — no forced entry at higher prices. The bigger bear case: Apple Intelligence 2.0 launch fails to drive measurable NPS improvement in third-party tests, reducing the iPhone upgrade narrative before Q3 earnings.
invalidation: Entry zone not reached by June 19 (conditional expires — do not chase above $300); OR Warsh FOMC explicitly hawkish AND 30Y closes above 5.10% (wait for $275-280 re-entry instead); OR Apple issues a delay or downscaling of the PCC Google/NVIDIA partnership within 30 days; OR $278 daily close if entered

outcome.outcome_label: Conditional entry expired — dip never materialized
outcome.note: Entry required AAPL to pull back to $285–295 on a post-FOMC dip by June 19. The June 17 FOMC was sharply hawkish (9 hike dots, 3.8% median, Warsh dropping forward guidance), but the simultaneous Iran ceasefire at Versailles produced a gap-up that kept AAPL at $300.66 pre-market June 18, counteracting the multiple-compression headwind. With June 19 Juneteenth making today the final trading session, the $285–295 entry zone is unreachable. No trade was executed; return 0.0%.
